source.citation: Guo, B., Hong, Y., Qiao, G., Ou, J., Li, Z. (2018). Thermodynamic modeling of the essential physicochemical interactions between the pore solution and the cement hydrates in chloride-contaminated cement-based materials. Journal of Colloid and Interface Science 531, 56-63.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), Tables 1-3 read on the page images (the signs of the constants are lost in the page text), and the text of pp. 58-59
transcription.note: The inventory, the molar masses and the reported pH and AFt plateau were typed into test/chloride_binding_reference.jl before this file existed and agree with the article. The Friedel's salt plateau is not printed; it is read off Fig. 1(b) and marked as such. The article's captions and body text disagree on the numbering of Tables 1 and 2; the captions are followed here.

csh_per_liter.description: C-S-H per liter of concrete in the model's initial state.

porosity_percent.description: Initial porosity of the concrete, percent by volume.

csh_specific_surface_area.description: Specific surface area of the C-S-H.

csh_site_density.description: Surface silanol site density of the C-S-H.

pH_without_NaCl.description: pH of the pore solution at a NaCl mass fraction of 0 %.

pH_at_5pct_NaCl.description: pH of the pore solution at a NaCl mass fraction of 5 %.

aft_plateau.description: AFt per liter of concrete once the AFm is exhausted.

friedel_plateau.description: Friedel's salt per liter of concrete on the plateau, read off the figure; not printed.

surface_reactions.location: Table 1, p. 57: primary surface site reactions of C-S-H at 25 C (constants from their ref. [16])

dissolution.location: Table 2, p. 58: dissolution reactions of the hydrates at 25 C (constants from their ref. [20])

hydrates.location: Table 3, p. 58: molar mass and density of the hydrates (densities from their ref. [39])

csh_formula.location: Table 2, p. 58: the formula of the C-S-H its dissolution is written for, 5(CaO)·3(SiO2)·6.3(H2O)

notes: Table 1, first row: -12.7 is the constant of the proton form, ≡SiOH = ≡SiO- + H+; written against OH-, as printed, the same surface would carry log K of about +1.3. The row is transcribed as printed.
Table 1, third row: the product is printed ≡SiOHCl-, with the charge of the chloride; the reaction is balanced.

Table 2: the constant of Friedel's salt is printed positive, 74.93, for a dissolution into Al+3 and OH-; it is transcribed as printed. The C-S-H molar mass of Table 3, 191.4 g/mol, is one third of the formula of Table 2, 574.1 g/mol.
Table 3 prints 100.9 g/mol for CaCO3; calcite is 100.09 g/mol. It is transcribed as printed.
